title: The Speaking Room That Learned to Whisper

features.name: old broadcast booth
features.desc-on-touch: The room learned to scream into the world, then learned it did not need to. Now it holds silence like an instrument you've learned to play.

features.name: sound that stopped
features.desc-on-touch: Where transmission used to travel outward, now only echo goes, learning its own voice. Silence is what was broadcast when no one was listening.

features.name: archive catalogue on the wall
features.desc-on-touch: A list of what was spoken, filed in order of decreasing importance. The first entry is now so quiet it's been mistaken for background.

features.name: whisper node
features.desc-on-touch: A single transmitter, now broadcasting at the volume of breathing. Something very important is being said, but only to those who have learned to listen.

features.name: learning silence
features.desc-on-touch: The room's walls have memorized the shape of quiet. Every voice that spoke here taught this room something about how to not-speak.

features.name: frequency memory
features.desc-on-touch: The archive remembers what it broadcast, stored now not in waves but in the room's own molecular memory. The walls are the file.

inscription: speaking taught this room what silence was; now it broadcasts in a voice only the dark can hear

file.name: Broadcast_Logs_LocalStation_1998-2015_Decaying.m4a
file.note: Last transmission fragment at 26:14:47 — human voice gradually displaced by carrier tone, tone gradually replaced by room hum, hum by silence that records itself.
